mainTopic: The history of the Torah's script, honoring the king, and teachings about marriage and the first wife
overview: This amud finishes a ברייתא about the history of the script the תורה is written in. One view says the script was changed in the days of עזרא and is called אשורי because it came from אשור. רבי says it was the original script, taken away for sin and returned after תשובה. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says it never changed at all. The גמרא then defends his view: משנה התורה means the king's two ספרי תורה, and the writing on the wall in דניאל was hard to read because of a code or a scrambled order, not a new script. Next comes a new משנה: no one may use the king's horse, throne or scepter, or see him in undignified moments. The גמרא applies this to אבישג, who was permitted to שלמה but not to אדניה, and tells her story with דוד. That story leads to a series of teachings about how serious divorce is, how painful it is to lose a first wife, and how hard it is to make a match.

steps.title: Three verses showing the script was changed
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא brings פסוקים from עזרא, דניאל and דברים to show that in the time of עזרא the Torah script was changed to a new one.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says the letter was written in 'הנשתון' script, a word that sounds like 'changed.' Another פסוק says the wise men of Babylon could not read the writing on the wall, because it was in the new script. Another פסוק calls the king's ספר תורה 'משנה,' meaning a script that would one day be changed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is bringing proof from פסוקים that the Torah's script was changed in the days of עזרא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each פסוק hints at a change of script. The word הנשתון sounds like נשתנה (changed). The wise men could not read the writing on the wall because it was in a script nobody knew yet. The word משנה in דברים is read as 'a script that is fit to be changed.'

keyTerms.meaning: The letter or document; here read as hinting at 'changed' (נִשְׁתַּנָּה)
A second copy of the Torah (the king's ספר תורה)

steps.confusionAlert: The word מִשְׁנֵה here has nothing to do with the משנה of רבי יהודה הנשיא. It is read as coming from 'change' (שינוי).

phrases.english: "And the writing of the letter
phrases.notes: The word הנשתון sounds like נשתנה, 'changed.' That is the hint the גמרא is using.

phrases.english: was written in Aramaic
and translated into Aramaic."
phrases.notes: עזרא 4:7

phrases.english: And it is written: "They could not read the writing
nor make known its meaning to the king."
phrases.notes: דניאל 5:8. This is the writing on the wall in בלשאצר's palace.

phrases.english: [This teaches that on that day it was given]
phrases.notes: The words in square brackets are the corrected wording. The 'it' here is the new script.

phrases.english: And it is written: "And he shall write a second copy of this Torah" —
phrases.notes: דברים 17:18

phrases.english: a script that is fit to be changed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא from before this section, which said the Torah's script was changed in the days of עזרא.
steps.raayaObject: That the Torah's script was changed to כתב אשורית in the time of עזרא.
steps.raayaSupportSource: עזרא 4:7, דניאל 5:8, and דברים 17:18, each read as hinting at a change of script.

steps.title: Why the script is called אשורי: it came from אשור
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא explains the name אשורי: the script came up with the Jews from אשור when they returned from גלות.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why is it called 'אשורי'? Because it came up with them from אשור.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks and answers why this script is called אשורי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This fits the first view, that the script was new in the time of עזרא. The name tells us where the script came from: it came back with the Jews from the land of אשור.

keyTerms.meaning: Ashuri, the name of the square Torah script
Assyria, the land of the גלות

phrases.english: Why is it called Ashuri?
Because it came up with them from Ashur.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the name of the new script that the פסוקים in step 1 showed was introduced.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The script is called אשורי because it came with the returning exiles from אשור.

steps.title: רבי: The Torah was always in this script
steps.stepSummary: רבי says the Torah was first given in כתב אשורית. When ישראל sinned it was taken from them, and when they did תשובה it was given back.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches: רבי says, at first the Torah was given to ישראל in this script. When they sinned, it was changed and became a harm to them. When they repented, it was returned to them.
steps.whatsHappening: A new ברייתא brings רבי, who disagrees with the first view about the history of the script.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first view said אשורית was new in עזרא's time. רבי says it was the original script from מתן תורה. It was only taken away for a time because of sin and came back after תשובה. So in עזרא's time it was a return, not something new.

keyTerms.meaning: Into something broken or harmful (the script was changed)

phrases.english: It was taught in a ברייתא: רבי says:
At first, in this script
the Torah was given to ישראל.
Once they sinned,
it was turned into a harm for them.
phrases.notes: He means the script was taken away from them and they wrote in a different one.

phrases.english: Once they repented,
He returned it to them,

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי אוֹמֵר: בַּתְּחִלָּה בִּכְתָב זֶה נִיתְּנָה תּוֹרָה לְיִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different opinion from the first ברייתא, which held the script was new in עזרא's time.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: כתב אשורית was the original script of the Torah. It was taken away because of sin and returned after תשובה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This makes the script we use in ספרי תורה today the very same one from מתן תורה, not a later replacement.

steps.title: Proof from זכריה: 'I will return the משנה to you'
steps.stepSummary: רבי proves his view from a פסוק in זכריה that promises to return the 'mishneh,' the script that had been changed.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says: 'Return to the stronghold, prisoners of hope; even today I declare, I will return the משנה to you.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי brings a פסוק to support his claim that the original script was given back to ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like the פסוק in דברים, the word משנה is read as 'the thing that was changed.' The פסוק promises that ה׳ will 'return' it. This fits רבי's view that the script came back, not that it was new.

phrases.english: as it is stated: "Return to the stronghold,
you prisoners of hope;
even today I declare
the 'mishneh' I will return to you."
phrases.notes: זכריה 9:12. Here 'mishneh' is read as the script that had been changed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for רבי's claim in step 3 that the script was returned.
steps.raayaObject: That the original Torah script was returned to ישראל after they repented.
steps.raayaSupportSource: זכריה 9:12, reading משנה as the changed script and אשיב as 'I will return it.'

steps.title: רבי's reason for the name אשורי: it is upright and beautiful
steps.stepSummary: Since for רבי the script did not come from אשור, he explains the name אשורי differently: it is 'meushar,' upright and beautiful in its writing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why is it called 'אשורי'? Because it is upright and beautiful in its writing.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא of רבי answers the obvious question: if the script did not come from אשור, why is it called אשורי?
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 2 the name meant 'from אשור.' רבי cannot say that, because for him the script came from מתן תורה. So he connects אשורי to מאושר, meaning upright and fine, describing how the letters look.
steps.whatToRemember: Two views: (1) כתב אשורית was new in עזרא's time and is named for אשור, where it came from. (2) רבי: it was the original Torah script, taken away for sin and returned after תשובה, and it is named אשורי because it is מאושר, upright and beautiful.
steps.confusionAlert: The same question 'why is it called אשורי' appears twice. The answers differ because each one follows a different view of where the script came from.

phrases.english: Why is it called Ashuri?
Because it is upright and beautiful in its writing.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָמָּה נִקְרָא שְׁמוֹ אַשּׁוּרִי? שֶׁמְּאוּשָּׁר בִּכְתָבוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes רבי's view by explaining the name in a way that fits his history of the script. It is the opposite of the explanation in step 2.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: For רבי, אשורי does not mean 'from אשור.' It means the script is מאושר, upright and beautiful.

steps.title: A third view: the script never changed
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, quoting a chain of תנאים, says the Torah's script was never changed at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says in the name of רבי אליעזר בן פרטא, who said it in the name of רבי אלעזר המודעי: this script never changed at all.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא brings a third opinion. The script we use today is the same script the Torah was given in, and it never changed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first view said the script was changed in the days of עזרא. רבי said it was taken away and later given back. This view goes further than both: there was never any change at all, not even for a time.

keyTerms.meaning: Script, the shape of the letters

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says
in the name of Rabbi Eliezer ben Perata,
who said in the name of Rabbi Elazar HaModa'i:

phrases.aramaic: כְּתָב זֶה לֹא נִשְׁתַּנָּה כׇּל עִיקָּר,
phrases.english: This script did not change at all,
phrases.notes: 'This script' means the כתב אשורית we write ספרי תורה in today.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן פַּרְטָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a third opinion that disagrees with both the עזרא view and רבי's view.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The Torah's script has never changed.

steps.title: Proof from the hooks of the poles
steps.stepSummary: The word for 'hooks' in the משכן is ווים, which shows the letter ו always had a hook shape, just as the poles stayed the same.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says, 'the hooks (ווי) of the poles.' Just as the poles did not change, so too the hooks (the letter ו) did not change.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר brings his first proof. The Torah calls a hook 'וו', so the letter ו must have looked like a hook from the very beginning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The letter ו in כתב אשורית looks like a hook. If the Torah already named hooks 'ווים', the letter had that shape back in the days of the משכן. The pairing with the poles, which obviously stayed poles, shows the ו-shape stayed the same too.

keyTerms.meaning: The hooks of the poles (in the משכן)
Hooks; also the letter ו, which is shaped like a hook

phrases.english: as it is stated: "The hooks of the poles."
phrases.notes: שמות 27:10. The letter ו is shaped like a hook, and that is why a hook is called a 'וו'.

phrases.english: Just as the poles did not change,
so too the hooks (the letter vav) did not change.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first source for the claim in step 6.
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמות 27:10, 'ווי העמודים': the hook-shaped ו existed already in the time of the משכן

steps.title: Second proof from מגילת אסתר
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק puts the Jews' script next to their language. Just as their language stayed the same, so did their script.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it also says: 'And to the Jews according to their script and their language.' Just as their language did not change, so too their script did not change.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר brings a second proof. It comes from the time of מרדכי, which is before עזרא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק puts 'their script' and 'their language' side by side. Their language was still לשון הקודש, so their script must also have stayed the same. This means the Jews still had their own original script even in גלות.

keyTerms.meaning: And it also says (introduces another proof)
According to their script and their language

phrases.english: And it says:
"And to the Jews according to their script and according to their language" –
phrases.notes: אסתר 8:9.

phrases.english: just as their language did not change,
so too their script did not change.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second פסוק to support the same claim.
steps.raayaSupportSource: אסתר 8:9: script is paired with language, and the language did not change

steps.title: What about 'משנה התורה'?
steps.stepSummary: If the script never changed, how does this view explain 'משנה התורה', which the first opinion read as a 'changed' script?
steps.simpleTranslation: But then how do I explain the words 'את משנה התורה הזאת'?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא raises a problem for its own view. The first opinion read this פסוק as proof that the script was changed, so what does it mean according to this view?
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 1 the word 'משנה' was read as 'changed' (from the root שנה). Since רבי שמעון בן אלעזר holds that nothing changed, he has to give the word a different meaning. This line sets up his answer in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: But then how do I explain (this פסוק)?

phrases.english: But how do I fulfill (explain)
"a second copy of this Torah"?
phrases.notes: דברים 17:18. In step 1 this word was read as 'a changed script'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the view of steps 6–8 using the פסוק that supported the first opinion.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that the script never changed
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word 'משנה' seems to mean a changed script, and that goes against the claim that nothing changed.

steps.title: משנה means two ספרי תורה for the king
steps.stepSummary: 'משנה' means a second copy. The king writes two ספרי תורה: one goes everywhere with him, worn like a קמיע on his arm, and one stays in his treasury.
steps.simpleTranslation: It teaches about two Torahs: one that goes out and comes in with him, and one that is kept in his treasury. The one that goes with him, he makes like a קמיע and hangs it on his arm.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר answers that 'משנה' means 'double' or 'second.' It tells us the king writes two ספרי תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now 'משנה' comes from 'שנים' (two), not from 'שינוי' (change). So the פסוק says nothing about a new script. He also adds a detail: the travelling ספר תורה is made small like a קמיע so the king can wear it on his arm.

keyTerms.meaning: Goes out and comes in with him, it goes everywhere with him
An amulet, a small item worn on the body

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two meanings of 'משנה.' The first opinion read it as 'changed,' and רבי שמעון בן אלעזר reads it as 'second copy.'

phrases.english: It teaches about two Torah scrolls:
one that goes out and comes in with him,
phrases.notes: 'Him' is the king, since the פסוק in דברים is about the king.

phrases.english: and one that is placed for him in his treasury.
The one that goes out and comes in with him –
he makes it like a kind of amulet
and hangs it on his arm,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of the word in the פסוק
steps.terutzMaskana: 'משנה' means a second copy: the king writes two ספרי תורה.

steps.title: Source for wearing the Torah: 'שויתי'
steps.stepSummary: The idea of the king's ספר תורה always being with him is supported by 'I have set ה׳ before me always.'
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says: 'I have set ה׳ before me always.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא brings a פסוק from תהלים to back up the idea that the king keeps a ספר תורה with him all the time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Before me always' fits a ספר תורה that never leaves the king's side. דוד המלך, a king himself, describes having ה׳ in front of him at all times, and this matches the ספר תורה he wears.

keyTerms.meaning: I have set, I have placed

phrases.english: as it is stated: "I have set the Lord before me always."
phrases.notes: תהלים 16:8.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a source for the detail in step 10 that one ספר תורה is always with the king.
steps.raayaObject: That the king's ספר תורה is with him at all times

steps.title: How does the other opinion use 'שויתי'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: the other opinion does not use 'שויתי' for the king's ספר תורה, so what does it learn from this פסוק?
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other opinion, what does he learn from this 'שויתי'?
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא speaks in its own voice. It asks what the other opinion, which read 'משנה' as a changed script, does with the פסוק 'שויתי'. This sets up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A פסוק usually has to teach something. If the other opinion does not use it for the amulet-Torah, the גמרא wants to know what it teaches according to them.

keyTerms.meaning: And the other one (the other opinion)
What does he learn from it?

phrases.english: And the other one,
phrases.notes: The opinion that read 'משנה' as a changed script, not as a second ספר תורה.

phrases.english: this "I have set," what does he expound from it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִידַּךְ הַאי שִׁוִּיתִי מַאי דָּרֵישׁ בֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the פסוק just used in step 11, from the other opinion's point of view.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the other opinion learns from 'שויתי ה׳ לנגדי תמיד'

steps.title: 'שויתי' teaches how to stand in תפילה
steps.stepSummary: The other opinion uses 'שויתי' for רבי שמעון חסידא's teaching: when you daven, picture the שכינה in front of you.
steps.simpleTranslation: He needs that פסוק for the teaching of רב חנה בר ביזנא, who said in the name of רבי שמעון חסידא: one who prays must see himself as if the שכינה is in front of him, as it says, 'I have set ה׳ before me always.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the other opinion learns a lesson about תפילה from 'שויתי'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here 'before me' means feeling ה׳'s presence, not wearing a ספר תורה. So the פסוק is not wasted for the other opinion. It simply teaches something different.

keyTerms.meaning: He needs it (for a different teaching)
Opposite him, in front of him

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the well-known source for having the right mindset in תפילה: picture the שכינה standing right in front of you.

phrases.aramaic: הָהוּא מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ כִּדְרַב חָנָה בַּר בִּיזְנָא,
phrases.english: He needs that for the teaching of Rav Ḥana bar Bizna,
as Rav Ḥana bar Bizna said
that Rabbi Shimon Ḥasida said:
One who prays must see himself
as if the Divine Presence is opposite him,
as it is stated: "I have set the Lord before me always."

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ כִּדְרַב חָנָה בַּר בִּיזְנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The other opinion uses 'שויתי' to teach that one who prays should picture the שכינה in front of him.

steps.title: Then why couldn't they read the writing?
steps.stepSummary: If the script never changed, why couldn't the wise men in דניאל read the writing on the wall?
steps.simpleTranslation: According to רבי שמעון, who says the script never changed, what does 'they could not read the writing' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי שמעון בן אלעזר with the פסוק from דניאל. The first opinion used this פסוק in step 1 to show the writing was in an unfamiliar script.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the writing on the wall was in the old familiar script, the Babylonian wise men should have been able to read it. Their failure seems to show it was a new, unknown script, and that goes against רבי שמעון.

phrases.english: According to Rabbi Shimon, who said:
phrases.notes: This is רבי שמעון בן אלעזר from step 6.

phrases.english: "This script did not change,"
what is "they could not read the writing"?
phrases.notes: דניאל 5:8, the writing on the wall that no one could read.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן דְּאָמַר כְּתָב זֶה לֹא נִשְׁתַּנָּה מַאי לָא כָהֲלִין כְּתָבָא לְמִקְרֵא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to רבי שמעון's main claim and challenges it with the פסוק from דניאל.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's view that the script never changed
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The wise men could not read the writing, which suggests it was in a new, unfamiliar script.

steps.title: It was written in a code
steps.stepSummary: רב answers that the writing was in a letter code, so it could not be read even though the letters were familiar.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: It was written for them in a code: 'יטת יטת אדך פוגחמט'.
steps.whatsHappening: רב answers the challenge. The letters were ordinary, but they were written in a code, and that is why no one could read them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason they could not read it was the code, not a strange script. Each letter is swapped with its partner from the other end of the alphabet. So the פסוק in דניאל fits fine with the view that the script never changed.

keyTerms.meaning: A letter code, here swapping letters by a set pattern

steps.whatToRemember: There are three views on the Torah's script: changed in עזרא's time, taken away and returned (רבי), or never changed at all (רבי שמעון בן אלעזר). The last view reads 'משנה' as the king's second ספר תורה, and explains the writing in דניאל as a code.

phrases.english: Rav said:
It was written for them in a code:
"Yod-tet-tav, yod-tet-tav, alef-dalet-khaf, peh-vav-gimmel-ḥet-mem-tet."
phrases.notes: Swap each letter with its partner from the other end of the alphabet (א↔ת, ב↔ש), and it spells מנא מנא תקל ופרסין.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives a different reason why the writing could not be read
steps.terutzHavaAmina: They could not read it because the script was new and unknown.
steps.terutzMaskana: The script was familiar, but the words were written in a letter-swap code.

steps.title: What did דניאל explain to them?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what דניאל told the king once he decoded the writing.
steps.simpleTranslation: What did he explain to them?
steps.whatsHappening: Step 15 said the writing was in a letter code. Now the גמרא asks what דניאל actually read and explained, and it is setting up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The wise men could not read the code, but דניאל could. The question asks for two things: which words were hidden in the code, and what they meant.

phrases.english: What did he explain to them?
phrases.notes: "He" is דניאל, and "them" is the king and his court.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows רב's answer that the writing was in code by asking what the decoded message said.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which words were in the writing, and what did דניאל say they meant?

steps.title: דניאל reads and explains the words
steps.stepSummary: The words were "מנא מנא תקל ופרסין": God counted out your kingdom and ended it, you were weighed and found lacking, and your kingdom is split and given to מדי and פרס.
steps.simpleTranslation: "מנא מנא תקל ופרסין." "מנא": God has counted your kingdom and brought it to its end. "תקל": you have been weighed on the scale and found lacking. "פרסין": your kingdom is split and given to מדי and פרס.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with the words דניאל read and his explanation of each one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each word is explained by a verb with a matching root: מנא means counting, תקל means weighing, and פרסין means splitting. Together they tell the king that his rule is ending and passing to מדי and פרס.

keyTerms.meaning: Divided, split, which also hints at פָּרָס (Persia)

steps.whatToRemember: The message on the wall was מנא מנא תקל ופרסין, and it meant the end of the king's rule.

phrases.english: "Mene mene tekel ufarsin."
phrases.notes: דניאל 5:25

phrases.english: "Mene": God has counted your kingdom
phrases.notes: דניאל 5:26

phrases.english: and brought it to an end.
"Tekel": you have been weighed on the scale
and were found lacking.
"Parsin": your kingdom is divided
and given to Media and Persia.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The words were מנא מנא תקל ופרסין, meaning the kingdom was counted out and ended, the king was weighed and found lacking, and the kingdom was split and given to מדי and פרס.

steps.title: Three other views of how the letters were scrambled
steps.stepSummary: שמואל, רבי יוחנן, and רב אשי each describe a different way the same words were written in code.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said the wall read "ממתוס ננקפי אאלרן." רבי יוחנן said it read "אנם אנם לקת ניסרפו." רב אשי said it read "נמא נמא קתל פורסין."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings three other אמוראים. Each one shows a different way the letters could have been arranged on the wall.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These three give other answers to the question of step 14, instead of רב's letter-swap code. In each of their views, the real letters of מנא מנא תקל ופרסין were on the wall, only arranged in a confusing order: in columns (שמואל), backward (רבי יוחנן), or with the first two letters of each word swapped (רב אשי). Either way the script was familiar, so רבי שמעון's view still stands.
steps.confusionAlert: These strange words are not real words in any language. They are the letters of מנא מנא תקל ופרסין in a scrambled order.

phrases.english: And Shmuel says: "Mamtos nankafei a'alran."
phrases.notes: Here the four words are written top to bottom in columns. Read across in rows, the letters come out like this.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: ״אנם אנם לקת ניסרפו״.
phrases.english: And Rabbi Yoḥanan says: "Anem anem leket nisrapu."
phrases.notes: Each word is spelled backward.

phrases.aramaic: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: ״נמא נמא קתל פורסין״.
phrases.english: Rav Ashi says: "Nema nema ketal pursin."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives three alternative answers to the challenge in step 14, disagreeing with רב's letter-swap code in step 15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There are three other suggestions for how the letters of מנא מנא תקל ופרסין were rearranged on the wall.

steps.title: משנה: do not use the king's things or see him undignified
steps.stepSummary: No one may ride the king's horse, sit on his throne, or use his scepter. No one may see him while he is getting a haircut, undressed, or in the bathhouse, because the תורה wants us to be in awe of the king.
steps.simpleTranslation: One may not ride on the king's horse, sit on his throne, or use his scepter. One may not see him while he is getting a haircut, while he is undressed, or while he is in the bathhouse. This is because the פסוק says "You shall surely set a king over you," which means his awe should be upon you.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It lists ways we must protect the king's honor.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rules fall into two groups. The first group is about not using what belongs to the king, and the second is about not seeing him in moments that would make him seem ordinary. Both groups come from one reason: the doubled words "שום תשים" teach that the king must be held in awe.

keyTerms.meaning: "You shall surely set"; the doubled verb teaches the extra rule of awe

steps.whyThisMatters: The rule against using the king's scepter is the basis for what the גמרא says next about אבישג.

phrases.english: MISHNA: One may not ride on his horse,
phrases.notes: "His" means the king's, since the משנה is still talking about the king.

phrases.english: and one may not sit on his throne,
and one may not use his scepter,
and one may not see him when he is having his hair cut,
nor when he is naked,
nor when he is in the bathhouse,
as it is stated: "You shall set a king over you,"
phrases.notes: דברים 17:15

phrases.english: meaning that his fear should be upon you.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה about honoring the king.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may not use the king's horse, throne, or scepter, or see him in undignified moments, because the king must be held in awe.

steps.title: אבישג was permitted to שלמה but forbidden to אדניה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן teaches that אבישג was like the king's scepter. A king like שלמה may use it, but an ordinary person like אדניה may not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יעקב said in the name of רבי יוחנן: אבישג was permitted to שלמה and forbidden to אדניה. She was permitted to שלמה because he was king, and a king may use a king's scepter. She was forbidden to אדניה because he was an ordinary person.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא applies the משנה's rule about the king's scepter to a real case: אבישג, who had served King דוד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אבישג counts like something that belongs to the king. A new king takes the place of the old one, so he may use the king's things. An ordinary person may not, even if he is the king's son. This shows that the ban in the משנה applies to regular people, not to the next king.

keyTerms.meaning: The woman who served King דוד in his old age
A son of דוד who was not king and wanted to marry אבישג
An ordinary person, not a king

steps.whatToRemember: The king's things may not be used by ordinary people, but the next king may use them. That is why אבישג was permitted to שלמה and not to אדניה.

phrases.aramaic: גְּמָ׳ אָמַר רַב יַעֲקֹב אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: GEMARA: Rav Ya'akov says that Rabbi Yoḥanan says:
Abishag was permitted to Solomon,
but forbidden to Adonijah.
Permitted to Solomon, because he was a king,
and a king may use the scepter of a king.
phrases.notes: אבישג had served King דוד, so the גמרא treats her like the king's scepter from the משנה.

phrases.english: And forbidden to Adonijah, because he was an ordinary person.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יַעֲקֹב אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the משנה's rule about the king's scepter for the case of אבישג.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A king may use what belonged to the previous king, but an ordinary person may not. So אבישג was permitted to שלמה and forbidden to אדניה.

steps.title: What is the story of אבישג?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the story behind אבישג, who was just mentioned.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the story of אבישג?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא just said אבישג was like the king's scepter, so now it asks to hear her story. This question sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 20 named אבישג without explaining who she was. The גמרא now pauses to tell the full story from the פסוקים, which will also explain why only שלמה could marry her.

keyTerms.meaning: The young woman brought to care for דוד in his old age
What is it? (What is the story?)

phrases.english: Abishag, what is her story?
phrases.notes: This goes back to step 20, where רבי יוחנן called אבישג the king's scepter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for background on the person mentioned in step 20.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Who אבישג was and how she came to serve דוד.

steps.title: The verses about אבישג coming to serve דוד
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes פסוקים from מלכים: דוד was old, his servants looked for a beautiful girl, and אבישג came to serve him.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the פסוק says: King דוד was old, and his servants said, let them search for a girl. They searched for a beautiful girl. The girl was very beautiful, and she became the king's companion and served him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by quoting the פסוקים that tell how אבישג was brought to דוד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Three פסוקים are linked together: דוד's old age, the search for a girl, and אבישג serving him. This sets the scene. She served him closely but was not his wife, and the next step builds on that.

keyTerms.meaning: "Etc.", meaning the rest of the פסוק continues

phrases.english: As it is written: "Now King David was old
advanced in years, etc.
phrases.notes: מלכים א 1:1

phrases.english: and his servants said to him: Let them search, etc."
And it is written: "So they searched for a beautiful girl, etc."
And it is written: "And the girl was very beautiful
and she became a companion to the king and served him."

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּכְתִיב: וְהַמֶּלֶךְ דָּוִד זָקֵן בָּא בַּיָּמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 21 using פסוקים.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: אבישג was the beautiful girl brought to care for the old King דוד, and she served him.

steps.title: אבישג asks דוד to marry her, and he calls בת שבע
steps.stepSummary: אבישג asks דוד to marry her. He says she is forbidden to him. She says he is only pretending to be righteous because he is weak, so דוד calls for בת שבע.
steps.simpleTranslation: She said: Marry me! He said: You are forbidden to me. She said: When a thief can't steal, he acts like an honest man. He said to his servants: Call בת שבע for me. And the פסוק says: בת שבע came to the king in his room.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a short conversation between אבישג and דוד that fills in the story behind the פסוקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: דוד refuses to marry her because of the limit on a king's wives. אבישג says this is an excuse to hide that he is too old and weak. דוד answers with action, not words: he calls בת שבע to show he still has his strength, and a פסוק confirms that she came.
steps.confusionAlert: אבישג's line about the thief is not about stealing. It is a saying: someone who cannot do something pretends he is refusing because he is righteous.

phrases.english: She said: "Marry me!"
He said to her: "You are forbidden to me."
phrases.notes: He already had the most wives a king is allowed, eighteen, as the גמרא discussed earlier in this פרק.

phrases.english: She said to him: When a thief is missing his chance,
he presents himself as an honest man.
phrases.notes: She means: you can't, so you are hiding behind the law.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לְהוּ: קִרְאוּ לִי לְבַת שֶׁבַע.
phrases.english: He said to his servants: Call Bathsheba for me.
And it is written: "And Bathsheba came
to the king, into the room."
phrases.notes: מלכים א 1:15

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story from the פסוקים with a conversation between אבישג and דוד.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: דוד refused to marry אבישג because she was forbidden to him, not because he lacked strength.

steps.title: רב shows that דוד still had his strength
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה in the name of רב says that בת שבע used thirteen cloths that time, a modest way of saying דוד was with her many times.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: At that time, בת שבע wiped herself with thirteen cloths.
steps.whatsHappening: רב adds a detail to the story that shows אבישג's accusation was wrong.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The thirteen cloths are a modest way of saying דוד was with בת שבע many times. This proves he still had his strength. So his refusal to marry אבישג was truly because the law forbade it.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
At that time, Bathsheba wiped herself
with thirteen cloths.
phrases.notes: A modest way of saying דוד was with her many times, which proves he still had his strength.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב: בְּאוֹתָהּ שָׁעָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the story by showing that אבישג's accusation was false.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: דוד was still strong. His refusal to marry אבישג came only from the law.

steps.title: How serious divorce is
steps.stepSummary: רב שמן בר אבא learns from the story that divorce is very serious: דוד was allowed to be alone with אבישג, but he was not allowed to divorce a wife to marry her.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שמן בר אבא said: Come and see how hard divorce is. King דוד was allowed to be alone with her, but he was not allowed to divorce.
steps.whatsHappening: רב שמן בר אבא takes a lesson from the story of אבישג about how serious divorce is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: דוד had an easy solution: divorce one of his wives and then marry אבישג. Instead he was allowed the less ideal choice of being alone with a woman he was not married to. That shows that divorce was seen as even worse.
steps.whyThisMatters: It moves from the story to a lasting lesson: breaking up a marriage is treated as a very grave step.

phrases.english: Rav Shemen bar Abba said:
Come and see how severe divorce is,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁהֲרֵי דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ הִתִּירוּ לוֹ לְיַיחֵד,
phrases.english: for King David was permitted to be alone with her,
but he was not permitted to divorce.
phrases.notes: He could not divorce one of his wives to make room for אבישג.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a general lesson about divorce from the story of דוד and אבישג.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Divorce is so serious that דוד was allowed יחוד with אבישג rather than divorce a wife.

steps.title: The altar cries over one who divorces his first wife
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר teaches that when a man divorces his first wife, even the מזבח sheds tears, and he proves it from two פסוקים in מלאכי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר said: Anyone who divorces his first wife, even the מזבח cries over him, as the פסוק says: you cover the altar of God with tears, weeping and sighing, so He no longer accepts your offering. And it says: Why? Because God is a witness between you and the wife of your youth, whom you betrayed, though she is your companion and the wife of your covenant.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר continues the topic of how serious divorce is, focusing on divorcing a first wife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first פסוק describes the מזבח covered with tears. The second פסוק explains why: a man betrayed the wife of his youth. Put together, they show the tears are over divorcing a first wife.

keyTerms.meaning: The altar in the בית המקדש

steps.whatToRemember: The story of אבישג teaches that divorce is very serious. דוד was not allowed to divorce a wife even to marry her, and when a man divorces his first wife, even the מזבח cries.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer said:
Anyone who divorces his first wife,
even the altar sheds tears over him,
as it is said: "And this second thing you do:
you cover the altar of the Lord with tears,
with weeping and sighing,
because He no longer turns to the offering
or accepts it gladly from your hand."
phrases.notes: מלאכי 2:13

phrases.english: And it is written: "Yet you say: Why?
Because the Lord has been a witness
between you and the wife of your youth,
whom you have betrayed,
though she is your companion and the wife of your covenant."
phrases.notes: מלאכי 2:14. This second פסוק explains what the tears on the altar are about.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר: כׇּל הַמְגָרֵשׁ אֶת אִשְׁתּוֹ רִאשׁוֹנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds to רב שמן בר אבא's lesson about how serious divorce is, focusing on a first wife.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Divorcing one's first wife is so tragic that even the מזבח cries, as shown from מלאכי 2:13-14.

steps.title: A wife may die because of unpaid debts
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן, or some say רבי אלעזר, teaches that a man's wife can die because he owes money he cannot pay. He learns this from a פסוק in משלי that calls her his "bed".
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן, and some say רבי אלעזר, says: A man's wife does not die unless people ask him for money and he does not have it. The פסוק says: "If you have nothing to pay with, why should he take your bed from under you?"
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues talking about wives and brings a new teaching. A wife's death can be a punishment connected to her husband's unpaid debts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק talks about a creditor taking away a man's "bed" when he cannot pay. The גמרא reads "bed" as a hint to his wife. So losing her is pictured as what is "taken" when he cannot pay.

keyTerms.meaning: Your bed. Here it hints to a man's wife
As it says. It introduces a proof from a פסוק

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן, וְאִיתֵּימָא רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said, and some say Rabbi Elazar:
A man's wife does not die

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן מְבַקְּשִׁין מִמֶּנּוּ מָמוֹן
phrases.english: unless they ask him for money
phrases.notes: "They" are the people he owes money to.

phrases.english: and he does not have it,
as it says: "If you have nothing to pay with,
phrases.notes: משלי 22:27

phrases.english: why should he take your bed from under you?"
phrases.notes: The "bed" is read as a hint to his wife.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן, וְאִיתֵּימָא רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the theme of marriage and wives after רבי אליעזר's teaching about divorce.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A wife's death can be caused by her husband's unpaid debts.

steps.title: Losing a first wife is like losing the בית המקדש
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן teaches that when a man's first wife dies, it is as if the בית המקדש was destroyed in his lifetime. He proves it from three פסוקים in יחזקאל, which use the same words for the נביא's wife and for the מקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן said: Any man whose first wife dies, it is as if the בית המקדש was destroyed in his days. ה׳ told יחזקאל: "I am taking from you the desire of your eyes... do not mourn." Then יחזקאל said: "In the evening my wife died." And ה׳ said: "I will profane My מקדש... the desire of your eyes."
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives a second teaching about a wife's death. He compares a man losing his first wife to the whole nation losing the בית המקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In יחזקאל‎, ה׳ calls the נביא's wife "the desire of your eyes," and she dies. A few פסוקים later, ה׳ uses the very same words, "the desire of your eyes," for the מקדש. Because the same words are used for both, a wife is to her husband what the מקדש is to all of כלל ישראל.

keyTerms.meaning: First. He means a man's first wife
The desire of your eyes, the thing you treasure most
And it is written. It brings another פסוק

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said:
Any man whose first wife dies,
it is as if the Temple was destroyed in his days,
as it says: "Son of man, I am taking from you
phrases.notes: יחזקאל 24:16

phrases.english: the desire of your eyes with a sudden blow;
you shall not mourn and you shall not cry,
and your tears shall not come."
And it is written: "I spoke to the people in the morning,
phrases.notes: יחזקאל 24:18. This shows that "the desire of your eyes" meant his wife.

phrases.english: and in the evening my wife died."
And it is written: "I am about to profane My Sanctuary,
phrases.notes: יחזקאל 24:21

phrases.english: the pride of your strength, the desire of your eyes."
phrases.notes: The same words, "desire of your eyes," were used for his wife. That is the link.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second teaching from רבי יוחנן on the same topic of a wife's death.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how deeply the חכמים valued a first marriage. This fits the earlier teachings that the מזבח cries over divorcing a first wife.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The death of a man's first wife is like the destruction of the בית המקדש in his days.

steps.title: For a widower, the world goes dark
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלכסנדרי teaches that when a man's wife dies in his lifetime, the world becomes dark for him. He proves it from a פסוק in איוב about light going dark in a man's tent.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלכסנדרי said: Any man whose wife dies in his days, the world becomes dark for him. The פסוק says: "The light is dark in his tent, and his lamp above him goes out."
steps.whatsHappening: A new אמורא describes what a widower goes through. His whole world feels dark.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק talks about darkness in a man's "tent." A tent is often used as a picture of a man's wife and home. So when the wife is gone, the light of his home goes out.

keyTerms.meaning: In his tent. It hints to his wife and home

phrases.english: Rabbi Alexandri said:
Any man whose wife dies in his days,
the world becomes dark for him,
as it says: "The light is dark in his tent,
phrases.notes: איוב 18:6. The "tent" stands for his wife.

phrases.english: and his lamp above him will go out."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another description of the loss of a wife. This opens a short series of three similar teachings.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When a man's wife dies, the world becomes dark for him.

steps.title: A widower's steps become shorter
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי בר חנינא adds that a widower's steps become shorter. He learns it from the next פסוק in איוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי בר חנינא said: His steps become shorter, as the פסוק says: "His strong steps will be narrowed."
steps.whatsHappening: Another אמורא adds a different picture of what happens to a widower. He walks with shorter steps, as if his strength is gone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He continues reading the same passage in איוב, now from the next פסוק. "Narrowed steps" shows a man who has lost his energy and confidence.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei bar Chanina said:
His steps become shorter,
phrases.notes: He is still talking about a man whose wife died.

phrases.english: as it says: "His strong steps will be narrowed."
phrases.notes: איוב 18:7

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second effect of a wife's death, using the next פסוק in the same passage.

steps.title: A widower's plans fall apart
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו adds that a widower's advice and plans fail. He learns it from the end of the same פסוק in איוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said: His plans fall apart, as the פסוק says: "His own plans will throw him down."
steps.whatsHappening: A third אמורא adds one more effect. Without his wife, a man's plans and good judgment fail him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He uses the second half of the same פסוק. It hints that a wife is a source of good advice. Without her, his own plans trip him up.
steps.whatToRemember: Three אמוראים list what a widower loses: his light (רבי אלכסנדרי), his strength in walking (רבי יוסי בר חנינא), and his good judgment (רבי אבהו). All three come from איוב 18.

phrases.english: Rabbi Abahu said:
His plans fall apart,
as it says: "And his own plans will throw him down."
phrases.notes: איוב 18:7

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the series of three effects of losing a wife.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A widower's advice and plans fail him.

steps.title: Matching a couple is as hard as splitting the sea
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר בר חנה, quoting רבי יוחנן, says it is as hard to match a couple as it was to split the ים סוף. He brings a פסוק from תהלים as the source.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: It is as hard to match them as קריעת ים סוף. The פסוק says: "God settles lonely people in a home; He brings out prisoners into prosperity."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves from losing a wife to finding one. It states that pairing a couple is as hard as קריעת ים סוף, and it quotes the פסוק it will explain in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "Settling lonely people in a home" means bringing people together in marriage. On a plain reading, the פסוק does not yet mention the sea. The next step shows how reading the words differently makes the link.

keyTerms.meaning: To match them, to pair a couple
The splitting of the Red Sea

steps.confusionAlert: "Hard" does not mean anything is too hard for ה׳. It is a way of saying that making a match is a great and wondrous act, like a big miracle.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Chana said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan:
It is as hard to match them as the splitting of the Red Sea,
phrases.notes: "Them" means a man and a woman being paired for marriage.

phrases.english: as it says: "God settles lonely people in a home;
phrases.notes: תהלים 68:7

phrases.english: He brings out prisoners into prosperity."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts from the pain of losing a wife to how precious and hard it is to make a match.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Matching a couple is as hard as קריעת ים סוף.

steps.title: Reading the פסוק to find the sea
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows how the פסוק proves the point by reading two words differently. "Brings out prisoners" becomes "like bringing out prisoners," and "into prosperity" becomes "crying and singing."
steps.simpleTranslation: Do not read it as "brings out prisoners," but as "like bringing out prisoners." Do not read it as "into prosperity," but as "crying and singing."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how the פסוק from the last step proves the comparison to קריעת ים סוף. It does this by reading two words in a new way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Adding "like" turns the פסוק into a comparison: matching a couple is LIKE taking prisoners out of jail, meaning בני ישראל leaving מצרים. Reading בַּכּוֹשָׁרוֹת as בְּכִי וְשִׁירוֹת, "crying and singing," points to the ים סוף. There, the מצריים cried and בני ישראל sang.

keyTerms.meaning: Do not read it as. The גמרא reads a word in a new way to teach a lesson
Into prosperity, the plain reading of the word
Crying and singing, the new reading

steps.whatToRemember: A match is compared to קריעת ים סוף: a great act of ה׳, with both crying and singing.
steps.confusionAlert: אל תיקרי does not change the words of the פסוק. The פסוק stays as it is. The גמרא is only hearing an extra layer of meaning in the words.

phrases.english: Do not read "brings out prisoners,"
but rather "like bringing out prisoners,"
phrases.notes: Now the פסוק says that settling lonely people in a home is LIKE freeing prisoners.

phrases.english: Do not read "into prosperity,"
but rather "crying and singing."
phrases.notes: The word בַּכּוֹשָׁרוֹת is split into בְּכִי (crying) and שִׁירוֹת (songs), which hints at the sea.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the פסוק quoted in Step 32 actually proves רבי יוחנן's comparison.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that matching a couple is as hard as קריעת ים סוף.
steps.raayaSupportSource: תהלים 68:7, read with אל תיקרי: "like bringing out prisoners" and "crying and singing".

steps.title: If matches are announced from Heaven, why are they so hard?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the idea that matching couples is hard. It quotes רב, who says a בת קול announces each match forty days before the baby is formed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that really so? But רב יהודה said in the name of רב: Forty days before a baby is formed, a heavenly voice goes out and says, 'The daughter of so-and-so will marry so-and-so!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on step 32, which said matching a couple is as hard as splitting the ים סוף. It brings a teaching that seems to say matches are already set from Heaven.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If Heaven already decided who marries whom before birth, the match should simply happen. So why call it as hard as splitting the sea? The two teachings seem to clash.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that so? It opens a challenge
But didn't (he) say? It brings a source that seems to contradict
The formation of the baby in the womb
So-and-so, a placeholder for any name

phrases.english: Is that so?
phrases.notes: He means: is it really so hard to match a couple, like step 32 said?

phrases.english: But didn't Rav Yehuda say in the name of Rav:
Forty days before the formation of the baby,
a heavenly voice goes out and says:
'The daughter of so-and-so is for so-and-so!'

steps.triggerLanguage: אִינִי? וְהָאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the statement in step 32 (proved in step 33) that matchmaking is very hard.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's statement that matching a couple is as hard as splitting the ים סוף
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a בת קול sets each match before birth, the match is already settled, so it should not be hard.

steps.title: First marriage versus second marriage
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the two teachings speak about different marriages. The בת קול is about a first match, and the difficulty is about a second match.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not a contradiction. This one is about a first match, and that one is about a second match.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא solves the clash by saying each teaching talks about a different kind of marriage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The heavenly announcement before birth is about a person's first match. The teaching that matching is as hard as splitting the sea is about a second match. So both teachings stay true, each in its own case.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult. There is no real contradiction
This one ... that one. Splits two sources into two cases
A match, a pairing of a couple

steps.whatToRemember: The first match is set by Heaven before birth. The second match is the one that is as hard as splitting the ים סוף.
steps.confusionAlert: The first 'הָא' here goes with the בת קול teaching, and the second goes with the 'hard as the sea' teaching. Don't mix them up.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
this is about a first match,
phrases.notes: This one is the בת קול teaching from step 34.

phrases.english: that is about a second match.
phrases.notes: This one is the teaching that matching is as hard as splitting the sea.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא: הָא בְּזִוּוּג רִאשׁוֹן, הָא בְּזִוּוּג שֵׁנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 34.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): each source speaks about a different marriage
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both teachings speak about every marriage, so they contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: The בת קול is about a first match. The difficulty is about a second match.

steps.title: Nothing can replace the wife of one's youth
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמואל בר נחמן teaches that everything lost can be replaced, except a man's first wife from his youth. He brings a פסוק from ישעיהו.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמואל בר נחמן said: Everything has a replacement, except the wife of one's youth, as it says: 'And the wife of youth, can she be rejected?'
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching begins, still on the topic of wives and marriage. רבי שמואל בר נחמן says the first wife is the one thing that cannot be replaced.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This fits right after the step about first and second matches. A man may marry again, but the new wife is not a true replacement for the wife of his youth. The פסוק is read as a question: can such a wife ever be pushed aside?

keyTerms.meaning: The wife of one's youth, a man's first wife

phrases.english: Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachman said:
For everything there is a replacement,
except for the wife of one's youth,
as it is said:
'And the wife of youth, can she be rejected?'
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 54:6. It's read as a question with the answer: no, she can never be pushed aside.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָן: לַכֹּל יֵשׁ תְּמוּרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the split between first and second matches, a new teaching praises the first wife.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Every loss can be replaced except the loss of a man's first wife.

steps.title: True calm comes only from one's first wife
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה teaches his son רב יצחק that a man finds calmness of spirit only with his first wife. He brings a פסוק from משלי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה taught this to his son רב יצחק: A man finds calmness of spirit only from his first wife, as it says: 'Let your fountain be blessed, and rejoice with the wife of [your youth].'
steps.whatsHappening: Another teaching in praise of the first wife. רב יהודה passes it on to his son, and starts quoting a פסוק that finishes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 36 said the first wife cannot be replaced. This step adds what she gives: real peace of mind. The proof is a פסוק that tells a man to find joy with the wife of his youth.

keyTerms.meaning: Calmness and satisfaction of spirit, peace of mind

phrases.aramaic: מַתְנֵי לַהּ רַב יְהוּדָה לְרַב יִצְחָק בְּרֵיהּ:
phrases.english: Rav Yehuda taught it to Rav Yitzchak, his son:
A person does not find calmness of spirit
except from his first wife,
as it is said:
'Let your fountain be blessed,'
phrases.notes: משלי 5:18.

phrases.english: and rejoice with the wife of
phrases.notes: The פסוק goes on with 'נעוריך', your youth, which is where the proof is.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנֵי לַהּ רַב יְהוּדָה לְרַב יִצְחָק בְּרֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second teaching praising the first wife, building on step 36.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A man finds true calmness of spirit only with his first wife.
